registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered on his instruction to close every closable gap, before any run of this test
hypothesis: The app's inflation forecast rule (AR on monthly y/y inflation, lag 0-13 by BIC, last 120 months), fitted at each origin on the consumer price index as it stood in that month's OECD Main Economic Indicators edition, has a lower RMSE than carrying the newest published figure on, 3 and 12 months ahead, scored against each month's first published figure. Every OECD member with saved editions, pooled.
knownLimits: Same model rule, benchmark, horizons and pass mark as cpi_forecast_realtime (US and euro area); this test widens the same question to the OECD members.
An edition is taken as out on the first day of its month: the OECD gives the month, not the day.
Inflation is worked out from the index in each edition (12-month change), as the app does with today's data.
Price indices are revised little, so this test is expected to differ little from the pseudo real-time one.
